```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(here)

census_dir <- here(
  "data",
  "census"
)

dir.create(
  census_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```



### TESTING WITH OHIO
```{r connection test}


# ohio process testing
ohio_census <- get_acs(
  geography = "place", # individual places, not counties/states (unless we want to do that)
  variables = c(
    median_income = "B19013_001",
    population = "B01003_001",
    poverty_total = "B17001_001", # total number of people in poverty in place
    poverty_count = "B17001_002" # people below federal poverty threshold
  ),
  state = "OH",
  year = 2024, # newest data from 2024
  survey = "acs5", # this is the ACS 5-year estimates
    # important b/c it includes smaller communities not covered by ACS1
  output = "wide"
)

# calculating the poverty rate
ohio_census <- ohio_census %>%
  mutate(
    poverty_rate = if_else(
      poverty_totalE > 0,
      poverty_countE / poverty_totalE * 100,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

head(ohio_census)
```

```{r adding_lat_long_ohio}
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# ohio geopgrahic boundaries
ohio_places <- places(
  state = "OH",
  year = 2024,
  cb = TRUE
)
head(ohio_places)

```

```{r generate_lat_long}
# generate latitude/longitude
ohio_places_projected <- st_transform(
  ohio_places,
  crs = 5070
)
ohio_points <- st_point_on_surface(
  ohio_places_projected
)
ohio_points <- st_transform(
  ohio_points,
  crs = 4326
)

coordinates <- st_coordinates(ohio_points)

ohio_points$longitude <- coordinates[, "X"]
ohio_points$latitude <- coordinates[, "Y"]

ohio_coordinates <- ohio_points %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, longitude, latitude)

head(ohio_coordinates)
```


```{r ohio_merge}
ohio_census_geo <- ohio_census %>%
  left_join(
    ohio_coordinates,
    by = "GEOID"
  )

head(ohio_census_geo)

dim(ohio_census_geo)
```

```{r validate_merge}
sum(
  is.na(ohio_census_geo$latitude) |
  is.na(ohio_census_geo$longitude)
)

sum(duplicated(ohio_census_geo$GEOID))

nrow(ohio_census)
nrow(ohio_census_geo)

ohio_census_geo %>%
  filter(
    grepl(
      "Oxford|Toledo|Cleveland|Columbus",
      NAME
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    NAME,
    median_incomeE,
    populationE,
    poverty_rate,
    latitude,
    longitude
  )
```

### NATIONWIDE
```{r national_data}
# ============================================================
# NATIONWIDE CENSUS DATA ACQUISITION
# ============================================================

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

# All 50 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C.
states <- c(state.abb, "DC")

# Create a folder for saved Census data
dir.create(
  "data/census",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Retrieve ACS data one state at a time
for (st in states) {

  file_path <- file.path(
    "data/census",
    paste0("acs_", st, "_2024.rds")
  )

  # Skip states that have already been downloaded
  if (file.exists(file_path)) {
    message("Already downloaded: ", st)
    next
  }

  message("Downloading Census data for: ", st)

  state_data <- get_acs(
    geography = "place",
    variables = c(
      median_income = "B19013_001",
      population = "B01003_001",
      poverty_total = "B17001_001",
      poverty_count = "B17001_002"
    ),
    state = st,
    year = 2024,
    survey = "acs5",
    output = "wide"
  )

  # Calculate poverty rate and add state abbreviation
  state_data <- state_data %>%
    mutate(
      state_abbr = st,
      poverty_rate = if_else(
        poverty_totalE > 0,
        poverty_countE / poverty_totalE * 100,
        NA_real_
      )
    )

  # Save the state's data
  saveRDS(state_data, file_path)

  # Brief pause between Census API requests
  Sys.sleep(1)
}

# Combine all downloaded states into one dataset
national_census <- purrr::map_dfr(
  states,
  function(st) {
    readRDS(
      file.path(
        "data/census",
        paste0("acs_", st, "_2024.rds")
      )
    )
  }
)

# Inspect the combined dataset
dim(national_census)

head(national_census)

# Count Census places by state
national_census %>%
  count(state_abbr, sort = TRUE)
```


```{r national_coordinates}
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# Download Census place boundaries nationwide
national_places <- tigris::places(
  state = NULL,
  year = 2024,
  cb = TRUE
)

# Transform boundaries to projected coordinates
national_places_projected <- st_transform(
  national_places,
  crs = 5070
)

# Generate representative points within each place
national_points <- st_point_on_surface(
  national_places_projected
)

# Convert points back to latitude/longitude
national_points <- st_transform(
  national_points,
  crs = 4326
)

# Extract coordinate values
coordinates <- st_coordinates(national_points)

national_points$longitude <- coordinates[, "X"]
national_points$latitude <- coordinates[, "Y"]

# Keep only the geographic identifiers and coordinates
national_coordinates <- national_points %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, longitude, latitude)

# Inspect the results
dim(national_coordinates)

head(national_coordinates)

# Save geographic coordinates
saveRDS(
  national_coordinates,
  file.path(census_dir, "national_coordinates_2024.rds")
)
```

```{r national_merge}
national_census_geo <- national_census %>%
  left_join(
    national_coordinates,
    by = "GEOID"
  )

# Inspect the merged dataset
dim(national_census_geo)

head(national_census_geo)
```

```{r national_validation}

# Total number of Census places
nrow(national_census_geo)

# Number of states and DC represented
n_distinct(national_census_geo$state_abbr)

# Check for missing geographic coordinates
sum(
  is.na(national_census_geo$latitude) |
  is.na(national_census_geo$longitude)
)

# Check for duplicate Census GEOIDs
sum(duplicated(national_census_geo$GEOID))

# Verify row counts before and after merging
nrow(national_census)
nrow(national_census_geo)

# Count missing median household income estimates
sum(is.na(national_census_geo$median_incomeE))

# Check for invalid poverty rates
national_census_geo %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(poverty_rate) &
      (poverty_rate < 0 | poverty_rate > 100)
  )

# Inspect state coverage
national_census_geo %>%
  count(state_abbr, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r validation_summary}
validation_summary <- national_census_geo %>%
  summarise(
    total_places = n(),
    states = n_distinct(state_abbr),
    missing_coordinates = sum(
      is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude)
    ),
    missing_income = sum(is.na(median_incomeE)),
    missing_population = sum(is.na(populationE)),
    missing_poverty_rate = sum(is.na(poverty_rate)),
    duplicate_geoids = sum(duplicated(GEOID)),
    invalid_poverty_rates = sum(
      poverty_rate < 0 | poverty_rate > 100,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

validation_summary
```

```{r census_value_checks}
# Check for invalid or unusual Census values
census_value_checks <- national_census_geo %>%
  summarise(
    total_places = n(),

    negative_income = sum(
      median_incomeE < 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    zero_income = sum(
      median_incomeE == 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    missing_income = sum(
      is.na(median_incomeE)
    ),

    negative_population = sum(
      populationE < 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    zero_population = sum(
      populationE == 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    negative_poverty_count = sum(
      poverty_countE < 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    poverty_count_exceeds_total = sum(
      poverty_countE > poverty_totalE,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

census_value_checks
```

```{r data_quality_flags}
# Create data-quality indicators
national_census_geo <- national_census_geo %>%
  mutate(
    flag_zero_population = populationE == 0,

    flag_missing_income = is.na(median_incomeE),

    flag_missing_poverty = is.na(poverty_rate),

    flag_incomplete_socioeconomic =
      flag_zero_population |
      flag_missing_income |
      flag_missing_poverty
  )

# Summarize the flags
national_census_geo %>%
  summarise(
    zero_population = sum(flag_zero_population),
    missing_income = sum(flag_missing_income),
    missing_poverty = sum(flag_missing_poverty),
    incomplete_socioeconomic = sum(
      flag_incomplete_socioeconomic
    )
  )
```

```{r quality_issues_table}
census_value_issues <- national_census_geo %>%
  filter(flag_incomplete_socioeconomic) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    NAME,
    state_abbr,
    populationE,
    median_incomeE,
    poverty_rate,
    flag_zero_population,
    flag_missing_income,
    flag_missing_poverty
  )

write_csv(
  census_value_issues,
  "data/census/census_value_issues_2024.csv"
)

nrow(census_value_issues)

head(census_value_issues)
```

```{r more_validation}

# Identify Census places with missing income
missing_income_places <- national_census_geo %>%
  filter(is.na(median_incomeE)) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    NAME,
    state_abbr,
    populationE,
    median_incomeE,
    poverty_rate
  )

# Inspect some examples
head(missing_income_places, 20)


# Count missing income values by state
national_census_geo %>%
  group_by(state_abbr) %>%
  summarise(
    total_places = n(),
    missing_income = sum(is.na(median_incomeE)),
    missing_pct = round(
      missing_income / total_places * 100,
      2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_pct)) %>%
  head(15)


# Check whether missing income is concentrated
# in communities with very small populations
national_census_geo %>%
  mutate(
    income_available = !is.na(median_incomeE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(income_available) %>%
  summarise(
    communities = n(),
    median_population = median(
      populationE,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_population = mean(
      populationE,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r standardize_names}
national_census_match <- national_census_geo %>%
  mutate(
    city_clean = NAME %>%
      str_remove(",.*$") %>%
      str_remove(
        "\\s+(city|town|village|CDP|borough|municipality)$"
      ) %>%
      str_squish() %>%
      str_to_lower(),

    state_clean = str_to_upper(state_abbr)
  )

national_census_match %>%
  filter(
    state_clean == "OH",
    city_clean %in% c(
      "oxford",
      "cleveland",
      "toledo",
      "columbus"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    NAME,
    city_clean,
    state_clean,
    median_incomeE,
    populationE,
    latitude,
    longitude
  )
```

```{r duplicate_check}
duplicate_city_names <- national_census_match %>%
  count(city_clean, state_clean) %>%
  filter(n > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

duplicate_city_names

nrow(duplicate_city_names)
```

```{r investigate_duplicates}
duplicate_details <- national_census_match %>%
  inner_join(
    duplicate_city_names,
    by = c("city_clean", "state_clean")
  ) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    NAME,
    city_clean,
    state_clean,
    populationE,
    median_incomeE,
    latitude,
    longitude
  ) %>%
  arrange(state_clean, city_clean)

duplicate_details

View(duplicate_details)
```

```{r duplicate_solve}
# Identify the number of Census records per city/state
census_match_counts <- national_census_match %>%
  count(city_clean, state_clean, name = "match_count")

# Add the match count to every Census record
national_census_match <- national_census_match %>%
  left_join(
    census_match_counts,
    by = c("city_clean", "state_clean")
  )

# Create a reference containing only unique city/state matches
census_unique <- national_census_match %>%
  filter(match_count == 1)

# Create a separate reference for ambiguous matches
census_ambiguous <- national_census_match %>%
  filter(match_count > 1)

# Check the results
nrow(census_unique)
nrow(census_ambiguous)

# Verify that no Census records were lost
nrow(census_unique) + nrow(census_ambiguous)

# Confirm unique reference keys really are unique
sum(
  duplicated(
    census_unique[c("city_clean", "state_clean")]
  )
)
```

### Saving everything

```{r save_files}

# Save nationwide Census data as CSV
write_csv(
  national_census_geo,
  "data/census/national_census_geo_2024.csv"
)

# Save as an RDS file to preserve R data types
saveRDS(
  national_census_geo,
  "data/census/national_census_geo_2024.rds"
)

# Save missing income records for documentation
write_csv(
  missing_income_places,
  "data/census/missing_income_places_2024.csv"
)

# Save nationwide validation summary
write_csv(
  validation_summary,
  "data/census/census_validation_summary_2024.csv"
)

# duplicate solutions
write_csv(
  census_unique,
  "data/census/census_unique_2024.csv"
)

write_csv(
  census_ambiguous,
  "data/census/census_ambiguous_2024.csv"
)
```
